tasks.summary:
I fixed the reviewer finding: the app's generated templates were rejected by the djLint hooks in the target repo, and now they pass. All 17 acceptance commands pass.

What changed:
- **`new-app` reformats the templates.** After applying the overlay, `toolkit new-app` runs djLint 1.36.4 on the generated app, the same version and `--profile=django` the hooks use, through `uv tool run` with UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER set. It then runs `djlint --check` and `--lint`, and stops with exit 2 if either fails. The blank lines left by the cookiecutter template's conditionals are gone, and the manifest records the formatted files.
- **Regenerated app.** The 10 templates the reviewer listed are rewritten, and the 4 H014 errors are fixed. Run from the target repo root as the hooks run, djLint 1.36.4 updates no files and reports no errors on all 19 app templates.
- **Checks so this can't come back unnoticed:**
  - The CI lint job now runs `uv run djlint . --check --profile=django` and `uv run djlint . --lint --profile=django`. The spec listed only ruff and makemigrations for this job, so this goes slightly beyond it.
  - `tests/test_overlay.py` has a new test that runs djLint `--check` and `--lint` on the app.
  - `toolkit/tests/test_new_app.py` has 6 new tests: the djLint version comes from the hook rev, the order is reformat then check then lint, generation stops on any djLint failure, and the lint job contains the djLint steps.

Results: `new-app --check` finds 0 differences across 104 files. The app suite passes 355 tests on PostgreSQL and on SQL Server, and the guard reports 0 failures.
notes: Reviewer finding (djLint hooks reject the generated templates) is fixed. new-app now runs djLint, at the version of the template's pinned hook rev (v1.36.4), on the generated app from inside app/ so app/pyproject.toml [tool.djlint] applies. It reformats first, then requires --check and --lint to pass. Run from the target repo root as the hooks run, on the 19 tracked app templates, djLint 1.36.4 updates 0 files and finds 0 errors.
The djLint run uses `uv tool run --from djlint==1.36.4` with UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER set, so it needs the uv cache or network, just as the uv add/lock steps already do.

The CI lint job now also runs `uv run djlint . --check --profile=django` and `uv run djlint . --lint --profile=django`. The spec listed only ruff and makemigrations for this job; I added these so CI catches what the reviewer found. djlint 1.36.4 is already a dev dependency in the app's lock.
The root .pre-commit-config.yaml is unchanged in this attempt. The S0 hooks and the app's ruff-format and djLint hooks are as written in attempt 2.
test_overlay.py gained test_templates_pass_the_djlint_hooks, parametrized for --check and --lint. It runs the djlint in the app venv on the app tree.

tasks.summary: S4.models attempt 3: the work from the earlier attempt was still in the owned paths. I checked it against the new S4.template fix-round-1 inputs and changed no files. Those inputs only touch templates, CI and the overlay tests; none of them touch models, settings or migrations. I rebuilt northwind_demo_dev from model/schema.json with `toolkit stage1 --schema-from auto --schema-only --replace` (28 tables, no rows). I then re-drafted with inspectdb into the scratchpad, not the repo; it produced 28 classes, consistent with the curated models. The legacy app (northwind.legacy, label legacy) has 22 managed models, one per kept table in rules.json. They keep the original db_table and db_column names. on_delete follows the rules.json relations and choices come from the rules.json lookups, each with its rule id cited. The Before Change data macros are implemented as audit stamps and the table validation rules as portable CHECK constraints. Every model has HistoricalRecords and an admin with ImportExportMixin and SimpleHistoryAdmin. resources.py has RESOURCES keyed by db_table, with the original column names. Every model has a factory. 0001_initial holds the kept tables and 0002 the history tables. In the pipeline, toolkit/stage1.py gains --schema-from data-model and makes auto pick it for xlsm, with 8 new tests on a hand-written two-table data-model.json fixture. All 13 acceptance commands pass: stage1 tests 52 passed, legacy suite 55 passed, guard 828 files with 0 failures.
notes: Attempt 3 changed no files. The S4.template fix round 1 changed only templates, CI (djLint steps) and tests/test_overlay.py, and none of that affects the legacy models or migrations. I re-ran every acceptance command against the rebuilt northwind_demo_dev.

The inspectdb draft went to the session scratchpad (inspectdb.py, 28 classes), never into the repo. The 6 schema tables without a model (for example Catalog_TableOfContents, Learn, MRU, NorthwindFeatures, UserSettings and Welcome) are the ones not kept in rules.json, so the 22 kept tables each have one model.

Data macros for S5: model/datamacros.json lists 20 data macros, and all of them are Before Change. There are no After Insert, After Update or After Delete side effects to hand to S5. The Before Change macros set the audit stamps (R-orders-031, R-inventory-028, R-purchasing-027); they live in legacy/audit.py and are tested in tests/test_datamacros.py. That file also covers R-orders-006, R-inventory-009 and R-purchasing-003.
R-orders-049 cites the AutoExec startup macro, which is a UI macro and not a data macro, so it is left for the feature stages.

S5 and S4.data need to know: the audit stamp name comes from audit.acting_as(name), with System as the fallback. Dataset loads must wrap the inserts in audit.keeping_loaded_stamps() so rows keep the stamps they carry.
Employees.Attachments and ProductCategories.ProductCategoryImage are attachment columns and are not modelled; the dataset leaves them out too.

This is an Access engagement, so the xlsm-only import_map.py and test_import_map.py do not apply. --schema-from data-model is covered by the toolkit tests on the synthetic two-table fixture toolkit/tests/fixtures/stage1/data-model.json.

In the pipeline repo, toolkit/commands/new_app.py, templates/django-overlay/* and toolkit/tests/test_new_app.py are changed in the working tree, and templates/django-overlay/core/ is new and untracked. These are S4.template's paths, not mine. In the target repo, northwind/app/northwind/core/ and northwind/equivalence/adapter.toml are untracked and belong to another task. Integrate should stage only the owned paths.

The --replace step drops every table in the default schema, including Django's own tables and django_migrations. That is why migrate --fake-initial re-applies the contrib migrations each time on northwind_demo_dev; this is expected for a schema-only scratch database.

tasks.summary:
I fixed the S4.review lens 2 finding. A dataset load now stores every cell exactly as the dataset carries it, NULL audit stamps included, and writes no load-time value, so equivalence on seed-2 is no longer broken or nondeterministic for the 20 units that output AddedBy/AddedOn/ModifiedBy/ModifiedOn. Three changes, all in the overlay's core/loader.py:
(1) The loading resource's do_instance_save() calls django.db.models.Model.save directly, the way loaddata does. The model's own save(), legacy.audit's stamps, does not run during a load. post_save still fires, so the history rows with reason 'import <dataset>' are still written.
(2) core/local/load_hooks.py (keeping_loaded_stamps) is deleted. The generic load_context hook stays, and its doc now says it must not change loaded values.
(3) Fixing (1) turned up a second, related defect, so the loader now clears each import field's default (NOT_PROVIDED). ModelResource copies a model field's default into its import field, and that replaced NULL cells. Seed-2 Products.ReorderLevel NULL was loading as 0, and NOT NULL columns with clock defaults such as OrderDate and StockTakeDate would have got the time of the load. A column the dataset leaves out still gets the model default.
The tests now check every cell of every seed, audit stamps included. The comment that skipped non-editable columns ('system-kept columns (audit stamps) may be filled') is gone. A test asserts that at least one NULL in a system-kept column round-trips, and a new test checks that two flush loads of seed-2 give identical rows. I re-applied the overlay with new-app --only core against the updated S4.models output. All 10 acceptance commands exit 0: 244 core tests pass, equivalence on seed-1 is ok with 52 units not implemented, and the guard checked 827 files with 0 failures.
notes: Audit stamps on load: a dataset load now stores AddedBy, AddedOn, ModifiedBy and ModifiedOn exactly as the dataset carries them, NULL included. The load calls the base django.db.models.Model.save, which skips legacy.audit.AuditStampedModel.save(), the way Django's loaddata does. legacy.audit.keeping_loaded_stamps() is no longer used by the loader. It stays in legacy/ (not my path), and legacy/tests/test_datamacros.py still tests it. S4.models may want to retire it or note that the loader does not use it.

Second defect, same cause: django-import-export copies each model field's default into its import field and substitutes it for NULL/empty cells. Seed-2 Products.ReorderLevel NULL was loading as 0. NOT NULL columns with clock defaults (Orders.OrderDate timezone.now, StockTake.StockTakeDate audit.stamp_time) would have got the load time, and Companies.StandardTaxStatusID would have got the Tax Exempt code. The loader now clears these import defaults, so NULL stays NULL. A NULL in a NOT NULL column is now reported as a row error (table, row, column, Django code; no value) instead of being silently filled. A column the dataset leaves out entirely still gets the model default.

Tests: test_loader.py now compares every cell of every synthetic seed (all field types, audit stamps included), asserts that at least one NULL in a system-kept column round-trips, and checks that two flush loads of seed-2 give identical rows. The old text_cells() filter that skipped non-editable columns is removed. No test was skipped, xfailed or loosened.
Upstream S4.models fix round 1: I re-applied the overlay with new-app --only core and re-ran every acceptance command against the current legacy models and resources. Nothing else changed.

Only PostgreSQL was exercised here. The loader change is dialect-neutral (Model.save and the import-field defaults), but on SQL Server, behaviour still rests on mssql-django's IDENTITY_INSERT handling, as in earlier attempts.

notes: Audit stamps on load: a dataset load now stores AddedBy, AddedOn, ModifiedBy and ModifiedOn exactly as the dataset carries them, NULL included. The load calls the base django.db.models.Model.save, which skips legacy.audit.AuditStampedModel.save(), the way Django's loaddata does. legacy.audit.keeping_loaded_stamps() is no longer used by the loader. It stays in legacy/ (not my path), and legacy/tests/test_datamacros.py still tests it. S4.models may want to retire it or note that the loader does not use it.

Second defect, same cause: django-import-export copies each model field's default into its import field and substitutes it for NULL/empty cells. Seed-2 Products.ReorderLevel NULL was loading as 0. NOT NULL columns with clock defaults (Orders.OrderDate timezone.now, StockTake.StockTakeDate audit.stamp_time) would have got the load time, and Companies.StandardTaxStatusID would have got the Tax Exempt code. The loader now clears these import defaults, so NULL stays NULL. A NULL in a NOT NULL column is now reported as a row error (table, row, column, Django code; no value) instead of being silently filled. A column the dataset leaves out entirely still gets the model default.

Tests: test_loader.py now compares every cell of every synthetic seed (all field types, audit stamps included), asserts that at least one NULL in a system-kept column round-trips, and checks that two flush loads of seed-2 give identical rows. The old text_cells() filter that skipped non-editable columns is removed. No test was skipped, xfailed or loosened.
